title: Deterministic Load Composer — microburst profiling, quantile stitching, and customer signoff flow
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a deterministic, tenant-aware load composer and validation playbook for Dedicated capacity that focuses on microburst behavior, quantile stitching of latency distributions, and a repeatable customer signoff flow. This ticket delivers the bench harness, analysis notebooks, dashboards, and the signed acceptance checklist used during enterprise onboarding. Goal: provide customers a reproducible path that demonstrates we meet committed throughput and tail-latency SLOs under their slice-weighted mixes and transient microbursts.
background: Current load tools exercise steady-state QPS and large sustained ramps but do not accurately capture sub-second microbursts and multi-tenant variance. Customers report tail variance during short spikes and want a repeatable script + artifacts for legal/contractual acceptance. This work complements existing replay drivers by adding entropy-seeded determinism, microburst folding, and quantile stitching to present a single, defensible throughput story.
design_decisions: Composer will accept a captured workload file (JSON lines) with request timestamps and tenant id; a seedable pseudo-randomizer makes the replay deterministic across runs.
Microburst profiles are represented as 'burst kernels' that can be convolved against base traffic weightings to produce realistic short spikes (10ms-1s windows).
Use quantile stitching: measure per-bucket latency distributions across multiple short runs and merge to estimate tail behavior for longer windows instead of running prohibitively long single runs.
Autoscaler soak tests will use a hysteresis matrix (scale_up_threshold, scale_down_delay, cooling_window) exposed as a table in run configs to systematically evaluate policy sensitivity.
All artifacts must be runnable as a self-contained playbook: bench-run script, terraform module for ephemeral infra, and a Grafana dashboard snapshot for customer signoff.
We will provide a minimal 'acceptance pack' document template customers can sign to close the dedicated throughput commitment.
deliverables: microburst kernel library (XML/JSON profiles) with 6 curated profiles
quantile-stitching analysis notebook and CLI summarizer
autoscaler hysteresis sweep script and result matrix
Grafana dashboard snapshot and a Prometheus scrape config for the runs
customer acceptance pack (PDF) and canonical run recipe
integration tests and a GitHub PR template for customer onboarding
acceptance_criteria: Run recipe reproduces a signed result across three independent runs on identical infra (bit-identical summary output given same seed)
Measured p99 under the agreed tenant mix meets SLA within +/- 5% margin for accepted customers
Microburst profiles demonstrate no more than X% increase in tail beyond agreed SLOs (thresholds captured in pack)
Autoscaler hysteresis sweep identifies a recommended policy that keeps tail-latency breaches < 0.5% during 30s bursts
Customer acceptance PDF executed and signed by the customer success lead and the customer engineering contact
test_plan: 1) Sanity: run small deterministic replay with seed=42 against canary cluster and assert identical summary across three runs
2) Microburst sweep: apply burst kernels (10ms, 50ms, 200ms, 1s) at 1x, 2x and 5x baseline and collect latency histograms
3) Quantile stitching: run short windowed repeats and stitch p95/p99; compare against a single long-run baseline to validate stitching error < 3%
4) Autoscaler policy soak: 30 minute soak with scheduled bursts to validate scale-up time and cooldown behavior
5) Customer canary: run customer-captured workload in isolated tenant slice and produce acceptance pack
telemetry_requirements: Expose tail-latency histograms with consistent buckets across runs
Record KV cache hit rate and effective batch size per request window
Autoscaler event stream (scale decisions, triggers, cooldowns) correlated with latency traces
Persist run metadata (seed, kernel, tenant-slice, infra snapshot) to S3 for reproducibility
rollout_notes: Start with internal canary tenants during the first two weeks
Expose recipe to Solutions Engineering for next-step customer trials
Require SRE oversight for any run that escalates peak infra beyond reserved capacity
After 2 successful customer signoffs, promote recipe to 'onboarding-stable' and add to Runbook library
